note: WITHDRAWAL PROPOSED 2026-10-16, reason: duplicate of case 10. Two findings, in order. (1) The recorded trigger cannot reach the defect, for the structural reason case 08 established: fts3EvalRestart walks the subtree of pNear, a phrase's most senior NEAR ancestor, so in a flat '"sun moon" OR "star sun"' every phrase has pNear = itself, a restart can free only the poslist of the phrase being fetched, and that phrase's pointers are stored after the fetch returns. The 2026-10-11 note said instead that fts3BestSnippet runs twice and all three fts3EvalRestart calls come after both of them; that was the same wrong kind of reason as case 08's. (2) Rewriting the trigger the way case 08's was rewritten does not produce an independent case. With (xx AND (pp NEAR/3 qq)) OR rr and snippet(), host ASan reports the read at sqlite3.c:164924 in fts3SnippetAdvance through fts3SnippetNextCandidate, fts3BestSnippet and sqlite3Fts3Snippet, and the freed object is an Fts3SegReader freed by fts3SegReaderCursorFree <- fts3TermSelect <- fts3EvalPhraseLoad -- the same instruction, the same frames and the same free chain as case 10's query measured in the same build. A two-token saved phrase moves the free to the 8-byte merged poslist (fts3EvalInvalidatePoslist) but not the read, which stays that instruction. Case 08 survives the same test because its consumer is a different function (sqlite3Fts3Offsets), its saved pointers live in a different array (aTerm[] rather than aPhrase[]), and upstream fixed the two separately, in 3.49.0 and 3.32.0. This case has none of that. No arm is re-run: there is nothing here that case 10 does not already measure, and case 10's own trigger runs both snippet() and offsets() on its query
